frame.origin: contact point under the body centre (the bottom it stands on; the point below it when airborne)

authoring: Generated by HeronIso.gameplayGeometry() from the same BODY/POSE/MOTION tables the bake uses. Do not hand-edit — re-generate (docs/art/rigs/birds/tools/build.cjs --write).
extractor_contract: per section: rig export -> this sidecar -> absent section = the creature does not support the feature (not an error).

fly.note: slow, deep beats; neck folded, legs trailing. Flies alone and in a straight line

glide.note: wings bowed, on the way down to the flats

takeoff.note: a crouch and a leap; legs hang, then trail

land.note: legs reach down first; ends standing (in water) or roosting (dry)

stand.note: still as a post, in the shallows

stalk.note: the slow wade: one step every 1.8 s. The page moves it this slowly or the feet slide

poise.note: frozen over a fish, neck coiled

strike.note: f1 the lunge, f2 the bill in the water (splashRig.js smallest burst at the bill), f3 head up, swallowing

roost.note: hunched and dry: a rock, a bank, a wharf corner, a treetop

WADE.note: stand, stalk, poise and strike are baked WADING: the pivot is on the BOTTOM and the water surface is baked_water_z above it, so the legs under it take the depth tint. Place the bird where the water over the bottom is inside depth_m at that moment of the tide; when the flat dries or floods past it, the bird walks or flies to where it is right. A heron on dry ground uses roost.
WADE.tide: the falling tide, low water and the first of the flood

STRIKE.note: poise -> strike is the hunt. The page rolls the catch at f2; f3 (head up) plays either way.
STRIKE.catch_species_note: small shallow-water fish; the game's species data names them

ROOST.note: Dry and hunched, neck folded down. The pivot sits ON the surface.

LAND.note: land() ends in stand when the pivot is in wadeable water, roost when it is dry.

GROUP.note: Alone. Two herons on one flat keep keeps_apart_m between them; a second that lands closer is chased (the page may play takeoff on the newcomer). It flushes early: at flee_radius_m from a walker or a boat it is gone, with a slow start.

ANCHORS_PX.note: screen offsets from the pivot at dir 0 (bill toward N); use HeronIso.anchors(dir,{anim,frame}) for the rest

FIELD_NOTES.species: Great blue heron, Ardea herodias: the heron of Maritime tidal flats, marsh edges and creek mouths from spring to autumn.
FIELD_NOTES.sizes: length 97-137 cm, wingspan 167-201 cm, mass 2.1-2.5 kg (the brief's figures; the rig draws 1.17 m and 1.83 m, standing about 1.1 m). To be confirmed against a field guide by title, edition and page before the look is called final.
FIELD_NOTES.marks: adult: blue-grey back and upperwing coverts, dark slate flight feathers (the two-tone wing in flight), greyish-buff neck, white face and crown with a black stripe over the eye running into a plume, yellow dagger bill, dusky legs. The neck streaking, the chestnut thighs and the breast plumes are not drawn at this size.

_excluded.states: No swoop, dive, float, splash, preen, peck, walk or perch. It does not swim or plunge; on the ground its walk is the stalk.
_excluded.looks: One look: the adult. The darker-crowned first-year bird is not drawn — absence is data.
_excluded.dry_stalk: stalk and strike are drawn wading only. A heron hunting a dry field or a wharf is not drawn.
_excluded.skinned_export: No skeleton / bindMesh / clips. This rig ships on the sprite-sheet route the herring gull is on today.
_excluded.sound: Calls belong to the audio lane: one hoarse croak at takeoff when flushed.
